teaching_suggestions: Continue to leverage your conversational and flexible teaching style, as it has been effective in fostering student engagement. However, consider incorporating more structured opportunities for students to share their thoughts during discussions, such as using think-pair-share or small group discussions before opening the floor to the entire class. This can help increase participation and ensure that all voices are heard.

While your pacing is adaptable and focused on comprehension, aim to clarify key points more explicitly during your explanations. For example, when discussing the final exam structure, consider summarizing the main points at the end of your explanation to reinforce understanding. This can help students better retain information and feel more confident about upcoming assessments.

To address the observed engagement levels, introduce more interactive elements during your lessons. In your future lessons, reflect on the moments when students seem less engaged, such as during lengthy explanations. Consider using formative assessment techniques, like quick polls or exit tickets, to gauge student understanding and adjust your teaching on the fly. This self-monitoring can help you identify when to shift your approach or introduce more engaging activities.

Encourage students to take ownership of their learning by providing them with choices in how they demonstrate their understanding. This can enhance motivation and engagement while catering to diverse learning styles.
